query: Why do some travel expenses get declined, and which factors contribute the most?

per_column.name: asset_category
per_column.rationale: Categorizes assets (hardware, travel_equipment, service) which is a reasonable reading of short_description/ci. However, the query is about why TRAVEL EXPENSES get declined; asset categories relate to procurement/inventory rows, not the decline-driver analysis. Only marginally useful for THIS query, though travel_equipment could help isolate travel items.

per_column.name: acquisition_driver
per_column.rationale: Values (standard_procurement, automated_generated, travel_related) are readable from short_description phrasing ('Automated creation', 'Procurement'). It gives a grouping axis, but it concerns how assets were acquired rather than why expenses are declined. The 'travel_related' bucket has some relevance; overall usefulness is limited for the decline query.

per_column.name: travel_expense_indicator
per_column.rationale: A boolean flag isolating travel expenses is directly relevant to segmenting the query population. But all sampled rows are asset/procurement records marked False, and there is no clear source evidence for how True is assigned; groundedness is questionable and the flag is a bare binary with limited analytical leverage beyond filtering.

per_column.name: department_origin
per_column.rationale: This is trivially redundant with the existing original 'department' column, so it adds no new analytical axis. Moreover the source_text samples do not expose any department signal (only short_description/processed_date/ci), yet confident specific values (Customer_Support, Sales) are asserted, indicating unsupported/invented values.

per_column.name: source_id_presence
per_column.rationale: A presence/absence flag derivable from whether source_id exists, so it is reasonably grounded. But it is a near-trivial null-check on an existing column and offers little leverage for explaining travel expense declines; likely near-constant and low-value for this query.

judge.rationale: The added columns are oriented around asset procurement/inventory (hardware categories, acquisition drivers, source_id presence) rather than the decline-of-travel-expenses question the query poses. Only travel_expense_indicator and the travel_related bucket touch the query, and even those are weak binary/generic signals. department_origin duplicates an existing column and asserts values not supported by the shown source text, and travel_expense_indicator's True assignment lacks visible grounding. Categorical columns tied to short_description are otherwise soundly readable, giving moderate overall groundedness but low usefulness for THIS specific analysis.
